title: Zero-bit decision step
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $x,y$ be Boolean words, let $bits$ be a Boolean selector encoding, let $P$ be a valid input-head position for $y$, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$. Given auxiliary tape contents $\tau_C,\tau_O$, positions $z_C,z_O$, an optional state $oq$, an output register $r$, and a Boolean tag $b$, if $\tau_O(z_O)$ contains false, then one step of the constructed machine leaves it in the waiting-decision state, changes $\tau_O(z_O)$ to true, and moves that auxiliary head to $z_O+1$, with the other listed configuration data unchanged.
